AFWD.justification: The forward calculation of a^((n-1)/q) mod n to verify the witness property

AREV.justification: The decomposition of n-1 into its constituent prime factors for recursive verification

CLINK.justification: The sequential linking of primitive root properties across the prime factors of n-1

ENGAGR.justification: The superposition where n is a probable prime but lacks a completed certificate

EVALF.justification: The discovery of a non-trivial factor or failure of the witness congruence

EVALT.justification: The condition where the witness a satisfies the Fermat-based congruence requirements

FFUSE.justification: The unification of individual factor proofs into a single validity statement for n

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the proof into separate verification paths for each prime factor q of n-1

IFIX.justification: The permanent recording of the witness a and the prime factors of n-1 in the proof tree

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-evident primality of the base case integer 2

TANCH.justification: The final validated structure that anchors the proof of primality for the target integer

VINIT.justification: The raw numerical value before any primality properties are asserted or verified

phase_2.split_input: The primality requirement for n-1 factors

phase_3.both_description: A Miller-Rabin probable prime state awaiting deterministic proof

steps.domain_action: Assume n is a probable prime based on heuristic tests
Compute the value n-1 for factorization
Record n-1 in the certificate structure
Branch into the set of prime factors {q1, q2, ... qk} of n-1
Recursively generate Pratt certificate for q1
Link q1 certificate to the current node
Recursively generate Pratt certificate for q2
Link q2 certificate to the current node
Reconstitute the complete set of verified prime factors for n-1
Select a potential primitive root witness a
Verify a^((n-1)/qi) ≢ 1 mod n for all factors qi
Witness property holds for all branches
Confirm a is a valid primitive root for n
Append witness a and the factor list to the permanent certificate
Seal the Pratt tree as a complete primality proof

phase_5.memory_mechanism: The tree-structured data store for prime certificates
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Depth-first traversal of the prime factor tree
